title: Track a gradient
summary: requires_grad asks PyTorch to track operations for automatic differentiation. backward fills the gradient of the scalar result with respect to the input.
introduction: requires_grad asks PyTorch to track operations for automatic differentiation. backward fills the gradient of the scalar result with respect to the input. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: requires_grad asks PyTorch to track operations for automatic differentiation. backward fills the gradient of the scalar result with respect to the input.

blocks.code:
import torch

x = torch.tensor(3.0, requires_grad=True)
y = x * x
y.backward()
print(x.grad.item())
blocks.title: Track a gradient

blocks.text: The result is 6.0. The local slope of x squared at 3 is twice 3.
